# Text labels

<!-- Generated by `coney-tools refs render` from research/references/text-labels.yaml. Do not edit. -->

The keys of the string tables scripts show text by: objectives (`HUDSetObjective`), tutorial hints
(`HUDSetTutorialText`), mission-failed reasons (`HUDLaunchMissionFailed`), button prompts
(`SetMsgHandlerEx`) and HUD labels. A script names one as `<table>.<key>`. `global.lua` builds
`GSTRING` and `LABEL` for every level and each level script its own `LEVEL<n>`, in all five languages,
keeping `GetLanguage`'s; Rumble arenas build `RUMBLE`; the front end's `config_strings_<lang>.lua` hold
the numbered tables the engine reads ([GUI: strings](../research/gui.md#strings)). Only keys, never the
text.

The level tables' key prefixes, read from what the keys are passed to (inferred): `MS_C<k>_<n>` a step
of chapter k's objective, `MP_<n>` the mission's main objective, `MB_` a bonus objective, `MF_` and
`FAIL` a mission-failed reason, `TT_` a tutorial hint, `LBL_` a HUD bar's label, `CS_` an announcement.

!!! info "What is complete"

    Every key of every string table on the disc is listed, with the scripts that name it. Keys no
    script names directly may be built at run time (`ObjectiveString`) or unused; keys with no languages are
    named by a script but defined in no table. A table of lines (`LEVEL95.ACT`) shows the ids its
    constructors give.

716 entries. Data: `research/references/text-labels.yaml`.

## Sources and evidence

Evidence levels used: confirmed-code, inferred.

- config_strings_<lang>.lua, passed to the engine by config_preload2.lua
- every script: the string tables' constructors and the labels passed to bindings

## Fields

| Field | Type | Hand-written | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | str | | The label as scripts write it: `<table>.<key>`. |
| `table` | str | | The string table: `GSTRING`, `LABEL`, `TSTRING` (every level), `RUMBLE` (Rumble arenas), `LEVEL<n>` (one level's own). |
| `key` | str | | The key in that table. |
| `meaning` | str | yes | What the text is for, in our words, where the key does not say it. |
| `ids` | str | | For a table the engine or the menus read by number or name (`GSTRING.HUD`): the ids it holds. |
| `size` | int | | For such a table: how many strings it holds. |
| `languages` | int | | In how many of the five languages a script defines it (0: used but never defined). |
| `defined_in` | list | | The scripts that define it. |
| `uses` | int | | How many places in the scripts name it. |
| `passed_to` | list | | What it is passed to, most often first: a binding (`HUDSetObjective`) or a script's own helper (`ObjectiveSetup`). |
| `used_in` | list | | The scripts that name it. |
| `source` | str | yes | Where the entry comes from: a script and binding, an address, a chunk. |
| `evidence` | str | yes | How we know: confirmed-code, confirmed-runtime, inferred or speculative ([evidence levels](../guides/research-workflow.md#evidence-levels)). |
| `notes` | str | yes | Our own short notes. |
